topic: How the sliding rocks of Racetrack Playa move
hook: Rocks in Death Valley leave trails across a lakebed, but since the 1940s nobody had seen one move.

scenes.narration: A team including scientists from the Scripps Institution of Oceanography fitted rocks with GPS and watched with time-lapse cameras.
On December 20, 2013, they caught more than 60 rocks moving at once.
Rain had frozen into ice just 3 to 6 millimetres thick. As the sun broke it up, light winds pushed the ice panels, and the panels pushed the rocks.
One tagged rock travelled 224 metres in one winter.

loop_line: Next time you see those trails, picture thin ice doing the pushing.
title: Death Valley's moving rocks: solved
description: Source: Sliding Rocks on Racetrack Playa, Death Valley National Park: First Observation of Rocks in Motion. PLOS ONE (2014) 9(8): e105948. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0105948
